Merge pull request #41 from 3cgbdg/fix/ai-suggestions-cooldown-and-match-race

Fix AI-suggestions cooldown math and match-ready navigation race

fix(frontend): stop ReactQueryDevtools from breaking hydration on every page

A live QA pass found that every route in the app hard-fails hydration on
a full page reload (dev only): React logs "Hydration failed because the
server rendered HTML didn't match the client" and the whole tree remounts
client-side, discarding the real SSR content in the process.

Root cause: ReactQueryDevtools was loaded via next/dynamic(..., { ssr:
false }). Next's SSR bailout for that component ("Bail out to
client-side rendering: next/dynamic") was propagating past its own slot
and discarding the entire page's server-rendered content (confirmed by
fetching the raw SSR HTML directly -- it contained only a
BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING marker where the real page should be),
which the client then couldn't hydrate against.

Fix: mount the devtools only after the client has committed, via a
useEffect-set flag, instead of ssr:false. That keeps it out of both the
server render and the client's first render entirely, so it never
participates in the hydration diff, while a plain next/dynamic (default
ssr:true, never actually invoked before mount) still keeps it out of the
initial bundle.

Verified by fetching the raw SSR response for /profile and /dashboard
directly: the bailout marker is gone and real page content is present,
and repeated hard reloads in the browser no longer throw the hydration
error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(backend): treat the AI-suggestions cooldown as a no-op, not a retry

Follow-up from a QA regression pass on the previous commit: the
log-and-rethrow added to processSkillSuggestions was too broad. The
24h regeneration cooldown (AiService.validateRegenerationDate) rejects
with a ForbiddenException on every call within the window, and
enqueueSkillSuggestions runs unconditionally on every returning
Google-OAuth login, not just new signups (profiles.service.ts's
findOrCreateGoogleUser), so this is a routine, deterministic outcome,
not a transient failure. Rethrowing it made BullMQ retry 3x with
exponential backoff and log at error level for something that isn't
an error, on a very common path. Short-circuit ForbiddenException
specifically as a normal no-op; everything else still logs and
rethrows so real transient failures still retry.

Also add regression coverage for both of the previous commit's fixes:
- ai-queue.processor.spec.ts covers the cooldown no-op, a genuine
  failure still retrying, and the success path.
- SocketContext.test.tsx seeds a stale "matches" cache and holds
  invalidateQueries unresolved to prove navigation now waits for the
  refetch instead of racing it.

And fix docs/qa/README.md's local-setup instructions, which told
readers to run `docker compose up -d postgres redis` — the actual
compose service is named `db`, not `postgres`; running the documented
command as written fails with "no such service: postgres".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: correct AI-suggestions cooldown math and match-ready navigation race

Three concrete bugs traced from user reports of "long AI generation",
"regeneration cooldown doesn't reset the next day", and "have to
reload after generation completes to see anything":

- Profile.tsx: the "Regenerate AI suggestions" button's disabled
  state used differenceInHours(...) <= 24, which truncates to whole
  hours, while the adjacent countdown timer used exact millisecond
  math. For up to an hour after the real 24h cooldown actually
  expired, the button stayed stuck on "Wait 24h for next generation"
  even though the backend would already accept the request. Derive
  both from the same nextAvailableDate and stop memoizing the
  disabled check on a dependency that never changes with the clock.

- SocketContext.tsx: onMatchReady invalidated the "matches" query and
  navigated to the new match's page on the very next line, without
  awaiting the refetch. matches/[id]/page.tsx redirects away
  (router.replace("/learning")) if the match isn't in its cached list
  yet, and isLoading is false the instant any stale cached list
  exists — so the navigation routinely landed before the invalidated
  list had actually refetched, bouncing the user straight back out of
  the match they were just sent to. Force and await the refetch
  (refetchType: "all") before navigating.

- ai-queue.processor.ts: processSkillSuggestions had no try/catch, so
  a failure (including the routine 24h cooldown rejection on the
  background signup-time generation) was neither logged nor surfaced
  anywhere, unlike processGenerateMatch's proper failure path. Add
  the same log-and-rethrow handling so BullMQ's configured
  attempts/backoff still retries transient failures.

Merge pull request #36 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

feat(frontend): show the product on the landing page instead of descr…

feat(frontend): show the product on the landing page instead of describing it

The page had zero images and never showed the app. Half the hero — the most
valuable space on the page — was a flat purple rectangle with a small
abstract mark in it. A visitor could read the whole thing and still not know
what using SkillSwap looks like.

It also led with commodity and buried the differentiator: the headline
features were AI matching, chat, and scheduling, two of which every app has,
while the one genuinely novel thing (AI writes a structured, multi-module
training plan for your specific pairing) appeared once as body text in step
two of "how it works".

Changes:
- Hero now shows a real match card — MetricRing, SwapAxis, UserAvatar, Card.
  These are the app's own components with example data, not a mockup and not
  a screenshot: theme-aware, crisp at any size, no 700KB PNGs, and it can't
  drift from the design system the way a stale screenshot would. (The two
  images already in public/ are unusable — an old AI-generated brain logo and
  an abstract graphic in the wrong palette.)
- The training plan leads the page, shown as an actual plan with modules,
  timelines, and resources.
- A concrete example swap replaces the abstraction. Labelled "an example
  swap", first names only — an illustration, deliberately not dressed up as
  a testimonial.
- Alternating wide feature rows break the heading + three-card grid that
  repeated four times. Section heights now vary instead of sitting at
  564/489/416/534.
- Chat and scheduling demoted to a lighter supporting strip, which is also
  where reviews finally get a mention — a shipped feature the page never
  named. That strip uses its own SUPPORTING_FEATURES list rather than
  HIGHLIGHTS, since matching now has a section of its own and repeating it
  would be redundant; the auth panel keeps HIGHLIGHTS.
- One primary CTA in the hero, with "free / no card / two skills" promoted
  from 12px grey to a real element. Log in already appears in the header and
  footer, so a second large button there only competed.
- Scroll reveals via IntersectionObserver, which stay inert until JS mounts
  so the page is fully readable without it — verified no opacity-0 in the
  server-rendered HTML — and are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Page grows from 2.6 to 3.7 screens. Still statically prerendered.

Merge pull request #35 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

feat: public landing page + logo rebrand

feat(frontend): rebrand the logo around the teach/learn swap

The old mark was a rounded square with an "S" in it and a floating accent
dot — the default app-icon template, and it said nothing about the product.
It also ignored the app's best asset: the teach/learn colour pair already
used across skill pills, match cards, and SwapAxis.

New mark: two circles, one accent-teach and one accent-learn, overlapping,
with the lens where they meet in the brand violet. That lens is the swap —
the shared ground between two people's skills. Solid geometry with no thin
strokes, so it survives a 16px favicon, and it's built from the same tokens
the rest of the product uses, so the logo and the UI finally match.

Wordmark drops to two colours (ink + violet) and loses the trailing "AI" —
a feature isn't a name, and it dates the brand. "SkillSwapAI" is unchanged
in metadata, page titles, and the footer copyright.

Hovering the header lockup rotates the mark 180°, which swaps the teach and
learn circles around the lens: the logo performs the exchange it stands for.

Applied everywhere the brand appears — marketing header and footer, in-app
header, sidebar, and the auth screens — plus icon.svg, which carries a
prefers-color-scheme block so the favicon tracks light and dark browser
chrome using the resolved sRGB values of the same tokens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): derive the site URL on Vercel instead of falling back to localhost

Checking the PR's own preview deployment showed the landing page emitting
<link rel="canonical" href="http://localhost:3000">. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL
isn't set in the Vercel project, so metadataBase fell back to localhost —
which tells crawlers the canonical version of the page lives on a machine
they can't reach, and did the same to og:url and the sitemap.

Resolve the origin through a small helper instead: explicit
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL first, then VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL (set
automatically by Vercel and stable across deployments, unlike VERCEL_URL),
then localhost for development. Those Vercel vars aren't NEXT_PUBLIC_, but
every caller here — metadata, robots, sitemap — is evaluated server-side, so
that's fine.

This makes a fresh deploy correct with no manual configuration; setting
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is now only needed to override, e.g. a custom domain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): add a public marketing landing page at /

The app had no public surface at all: / redirected straight to /auth/login,
so a first-time visitor could never see what the product is, there was
nothing to share, and there was no SEO surface.

Adds a (marketing) route group owning / with a sticky header (logo, theme
toggle, Log in, Sign up), a hero, the three feature cards, a three-step
"how it works", a closing CTA, and a footer. Signed-in visitors still
redirect to /dashboard and never see it.

Copy is grounded only in shipped functionality — AI matching, AI-generated
training plans, chat, scheduling, and post-session reviews. No invented
testimonials, logo walls, or user-count stats.

Notes on the shape:
- A route group rather than a bare app/page.tsx, so terms/privacy can reuse
  the header/footer later; this is also the documented way to own / when
  every page lives in a group.
- Marketing components hold every rounded/shadowed/bordered surface, because
  the repo's ESLint layering rule bans those utilities inline under
  src/app/**. The route files stay composition plus design tokens.
- No components/marketing/index.ts barrel: knip's ignoreIssues doesn't cover
  that directory, so a re-exported-but-internally-consumed component would
  be flagged unused.
- Reuses the existing Container, Logo, SkillSwapMark, Card, Badge, and
  buttonVariants rather than adding new primitives.
- Middleware grows a PUBLIC_PATHS allowlist instead of hardcoding /, so
  future public routes don't get caught by the logged-out redirect. The
  matcher already excludes dotted paths, so robots.txt and sitemap.xml are
  served without passing through it.
- middleware is deprecated in favour of proxy in this Next version; left as
  middleware.ts here to keep the rename out of an unrelated change.

Verified in a browser: logged out / renders with no 401s and no toast;
Log in navigates to /auth/login; with a session / and /auth/login both 307
to /dashboard; logged-out /dashboard still 307s to /auth/login;
robots.txt and sitemap.xml both 200. Contrast checker 44/44, and the
production build prerenders / as static.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(frontend): extract shared product copy into marketing/content.ts

The tagline, subheadline, and the three feature blurbs were inlined in
AuthSplitPane. The landing page needs the same words, so pull them into a
plain data module both surfaces import — sharing the copy is what actually
prevents drift.

Deliberately shares copy, not markup: the auth panel is an inverted
bg-primary half-screen column hidden below lg, while the landing hero is a
full-bleed two-column section. A shared component would need a variant prop
threaded through spacing, typography, and visibility for no real gain.

content.ts has no "use client" and no JSX so server components can consume
it directly; lucide icon references are hook-free and RSC-safe.

AuthSplitPane's markup, classNames, and "use client" directive are
unchanged — an import swap and three identifier substitutions. Verified the
rendered headline, subheadline, and all three highlight title/description
pairs are identical before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): stop authenticated queries firing on public and auth pages

SocketProvider sat in the root layout, and SocketContext calls useProfile()
and useChats() unguarded at the top of its body. That meant every page under
the root layout — including the auth screens — fired GET /auth/profile and
GET /chats on mount. Logged out those 401, triggering a silent /auth/refresh
that also 401s, and the toast gate in axiosInstance only exempted
/auth/login and /auth/signup by exact equality. So /auth/forgot-password
already greeted logged-out visitors with an "Unauthorized" error toast, and
any new public route would have done the same.

Move SocketProvider down into (main)/layout.tsx, where it belongs: sockets,
the profile, and the chat list are all authenticated-app concerns. Verified
every consumer of socket/profile/chat state is under (main) — Header,
Matches, CalendarPopup, chats/[id], and useOnlineUsers via ChatSidebar — and
SocketContext defaults to { socket: null }, so anything rendered outside the
provider degrades rather than throwing. QueryProvider stays at the root, so
the provider is still below it; Toaster stays too, so auth toasts still work.

Also widen the axios 401-toast exemption from exact equality to "/" plus any
/auth path, as defence in depth for future public routes.

Verified: logged out on /auth/forgot-password now makes zero backend
requests and logs nothing, where before it fired three and toasted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #34 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

confirmed the click now actually navigates the browser to the target
URL (a real connection-refused error page), where before nothing
happened at all.

Merge pull request #33 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

Add post-session ratings and reviews

feat(frontend): add ratings/reviews UI

New StarRating composite (read-only and interactive modes, no rating
primitive existed anywhere in the codebase) and RateSessionDialog for
submitting a 1-5 star rating with an optional comment.

ProfileView gets a new Reviews section — average rating, review count,
and the review list — fetched separately via useUserReviews so it can
page independently of the profile itself; wired into both the own-
profile and public-profile pages.

The Schedule page gets a new "Past sessions to rate" section, driven by
useReviewableSessions (already server-filtered to ended/agreed/not-yet-
reviewed, no client-side date filtering needed); submitting a review
invalidates the list so the card disappears immediately.

SocketContext listens for the new reviewPrompt event (toast + cache
invalidation), following the same on/off pattern as the existing
matchReady/matchFailed listeners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(backend): add reviews module, session-end sweep, and profile ratings

New /reviews module:
- POST /reviews — full authorization chain: caller must be a session
  participant, the session must be AGREED and already ended, and a
  reviewer can only review a given session once (checked pre-emptively
  for a clean 409, backed by a DB unique constraint). revieweeId is
  derived server-side from the session's participants, never client-
  supplied, so a caller can't target an arbitrary user.
- GET /reviews/user/:id — paginated reviews + aggregate rating for a
  profile, kept separate from the profile fetch so the list can page
  independently.
- GET /reviews/reviewable-sessions — the caller's own past, agreed,
  not-yet-reviewed sessions, reusing SessionsUtils.mapSessionWithFriend
  for a shape the frontend already knows how to render.

New session-end sweep (ReviewPromptService, mirrors AutoAcceptService's
advisory-lock + cursor-paginated-batch pattern, registered directly in
QueuesModule to match how AutoAcceptService is actually wired rather
than the empty, unused TasksModule): every 60s, finds AGREED sessions
past endsAt that haven't been prompted yet, notifies both participants
over the existing cache-and-replay socket pattern, and stamps
reviewPromptedAt so it's never re-swept.

GET /auth/profile and GET /profiles/:id now include averageRating and
reviewCount alongside the existing profile data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(backend): add Review model and migration

Adds a Review model for post-session ratings: a reviewer/reviewee pair
(reusing Match's two-sided relation naming), one review per session per
reviewer enforced via a unique constraint, and a Session.reviewPromptedAt
flag for the sweep job that will notify participants once a session ends.

A real-time aggregate (Prisma's review.aggregate) is used for average
rating/review count rather than a denormalized counter on User —
User.completedSessionsCount already sits unused in this schema as a
cautionary example of exactly that failure mode.

Includes a follow-up migration restoring two trigram search indexes
(User.name, Skill.title) that `prisma migrate dev` drops as undeclared
"drift" on every run, since Prisma's schema DSL here can't represent GIN
trigram indexes — the same trap already documented and fixed once before
in this migration history. Applied via `migrate deploy`, not `migrate
dev`, so it isn't immediately re-dropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #32 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

UI consistency pass + full logic/security review

fix(frontend): fetch a full upcoming-sessions window and fix calendar popover

Dashboard's "Next up" and the Schedule page's "Upcoming sessions" both
called /sessions/today, so a session booked for any day other than
today never appeared there — despite showing correctly on the calendar
grid itself. Now fetches a year-forward window via the existing ranged
endpoint; the now-unused getTodaysSessions wrapper is removed.

Also fixes two bugs in the calendar's session-details popover: the
trigger nested a real <button> inside another real <button> (invalid
HTML, causing a React hydration error), and the button appeared even
for sessions with an empty-string description, opening a blank popover
with no way to close it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): link match and chat avatars to profiles, hide inactionable remove-picture button

The hover-preview trigger around match-card and chat-header avatars is
a Base UI PreviewCard.Trigger, which renders as a real <a> element —
but neither passed an href, so clicking the avatar did nothing. Now
links directly to the person's profile; MatchCard's redundant
hover-only "View profile" link is no longer needed.

Also hides the "Remove Picture" button on the profile edit page when
there's no avatar set — it was always rendered regardless, and
clicking it with no image to remove produced a confusing outcome for
an action that had nothing to do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): clear the AI match-generation banner when the job fails

The "Generating your AI training plan" banner and its 5s poll loop
only cleared on success. If generation failed server-side, the banner
stayed stuck showing "Generating..." indefinitely (and kept polling
forever) even after a "Failed to generate match" toast had already
appeared. Now listens for the matchFailed socket event and resets the
pending state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): clear query cache on auth and gate routes with middleware

Login and signup only invalidated the "profile" query, which doesn't
force a refetch for a query with no active observer — the dashboard
briefly rendered stale/errored pre-auth state (0% profile, missing
name, a wrongly-shown onboarding wizard) until a manual reload. Now
uses queryClient.clear(), matching the pattern already used on logout.

Also replaces the client-side CheckEmptyPath hack — which blindly
redirected "/" to "/dashboard" with no auth check at all, after the
server had already rendered a real 404 for the unauthenticated
request — with proper middleware: "/" now redirects based on session
state, protected routes redirect to /auth/login when logged out, and
/auth/* redirects to /dashboard when already logged in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(backend): raise default rate limit and stop leaking internal errors

The global short-tier throttle (3 requests/10s) applied to every route
by default and was tight enough that normal SPA navigation — a
dashboard load alone fires 5+ parallel GETs — would 429 real users.
Sensitive routes already had their own tighter per-route overrides, so
this only loosens the catch-all default; raised to 30/10s.

The catch-all exception filter also echoed a raw Error's message back
to the client for any unhandled exception, potentially leaking
internal details (DB/driver errors, third-party SDK internals). Now
logs the real message server-side but responds with a generic message.

Also logs failures to enqueue AI skill-suggestion generation instead
of silently swallowing them — a Redis hiccup during signup previously
left new users without suggestions with no trace of why.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(backend): require ownership before mutating friends, requests, sessions, plans, and chats

A consistent pattern across several modules: an endpoint checked that
the caller was authenticated, but not that they actually owned or were
party to the resource being read or mutated.

- POST /friends created a "friendship" from any caller-supplied user ID
  without ever checking a pending request existed from that user.
- DELETE /requests/:id deleted any request by ID with no check that the
  caller sent or received it.
- GET /plans/:id and the module-complete endpoint didn't check the
  caller was a participant of the underlying match — completing the
  last module also deletes the match, making this a data-destruction
  path, not just a read.
- Accepting/rejecting a session request only checked the caller was a
  participant of *some* session, not that the requestId belonged to
  that session or was addressed to them — letting a participant of any
  session delete an unrelated pending request belonging to someone else.
- The chat lookup used Prisma's `every` filter, which is vacuously true
  against a chat with only one participant (producible via the bot
  re-seed flow, which deletes bot users without cleaning up their chat
  rows) — fixed to require both participants independently.
- The WebSocket `updateSeen` handler updated a message's read state by
  ID with no check the caller was the recipient.
- Match/AI-plan generation didn't require friendship, even though the
  UI only exposes it for friends — anyone could burn AI-generation
  quota against an arbitrary user.

All fixes covered by new regression tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(backend): verify refresh-token signature and remove login enumeration

The /auth/refresh endpoint decoded the refresh token without verifying
its signature and was gated behind a guard that required an already-
valid access token to even reach it. Together this meant the refresh
flow could never do its actual job (recovering a session once the
15-minute access token expires), and if that guard were ever loosened,
an attacker could forge an arbitrary unsigned refresh token to mint a
valid access token for any user ID.

Now verifies the token against JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, confirms the user
still exists, and no longer requires a live access token to call.

Also fixes login returning 404 for an unknown email vs 401 for a wrong
password, which let a caller enumerate registered emails by status
code alone even though the message text was identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #31 from 3cgbdg/ui/full-review-consistency-pass

Full UI/UX consistency review and fixes

fix(frontend): unify match compatibility display, dedupe inbox loading

DashboardMatchCard showed compatibility as a plain "X% match" Badge
while the discover/matches MatchCard showed the identical data as a
MetricRing (circular indicator) — same real-world value, two unrelated
treatments depending on which screen it appeared on. Standardize on
MetricRing.

InboxRequestsPanel had its own hand-rolled loading branch (an early
return with a bare Spinner) sitting in front of AsyncBoundary, which
it also uses — two different boundary mechanisms doing overlapping
jobs. Fold the loading state into AsyncBoundary's own isLoading prop
like every other AsyncBoundary user in the app.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): remove duplicate calendar header, unify chat panel height Calendar.tsx rendered its own

Calendar

+ subtitle + action row inside the page, even though schedule/page.tsx already renders PageHeader title="Schedule" above it — the rendered page had two h1-styled headings stacked. Drop the duplicate heading, keep the week range/nav/new-session row as a lightweight toolbar under the real page title. Also add missing focus-visible/hover states to CalendarPopup's color swatch buttons, which had none at all. Separately: the chat panel's min-height formula (100dvh - header-h - space-page*2, with a further offset for desktop) was hand-duplicated across three files with three different offsets (0, 3.25rem, 4.5rem extra), clearly hand-tuned independently rather than derived from one source. Extract --chat-panel-min-h / --chat-panel-min-h-md custom properties in globals.css and reference them from layout.tsx, ChatThread.tsx, and SkeletonKit's chat skeleton so there's exactly one formula instead of three. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5

fix(frontend): stop fighting the Card spacing system on profile/match screens

Several cards manually zeroed out CardHeader/CardContent padding
(p-0) and replaced it with one-off outer padding (p-8, p-6,
pt-[21px]) and gaps (gap-7) not used anywhere else in the app, instead
of using the Card component's own --card-spacing scale that every
other card in the app relies on:

- matches/[id]/page.tsx: three cards (AI plan hero, partner-actions
  card, training-modules card) had their own magic-number
  padding/gaps; let them use Card's default spacing like everywhere
  else. Also fixed a stray gap-5 on the message/schedule buttons to
  match the gap-2 used for every other icon+label button.
- profile/EditProfile.tsx: replaced a hand-rolled <h1> + button row
  that duplicated PageHeader's own title/description/actions with the
  actual PageHeader composite, and removed the same p-6/p-0 pattern
  from its two cards.
- profile/AddSkills.tsx: removed pt-[21px] (an arbitrary pixel value
  eyeballed to nudge the title baseline) and the same p-0 overrides.
- profiles/[id]/page.tsx: same gap-5 -> gap-2 button fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): make auth screens visually consistent

The auth card used shadow-lg — the heaviest shadow in the design
system (--elev-shadow-lg), used nowhere else in the app, which nothing
else ever reaches above shadow-sm/shadow-md via the Card elevation
system. Switch to elevation="raised" (bg-surface-raised + shadow-sm)
to match how every other elevated surface in the app looks.

Forgot-password was also missing AuthBrand entirely and used a flatter
card with different padding than Login/Signup, so a user bouncing from
Login to "forgot password" mid-flow saw the logo/wordmark disappear
and the card's weight visibly change. Bring it in line with the same
AuthBrand + elevation + max-w-lg + pt-10 treatment as Login/Signup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #28 from 3cgbdg/hotfix/bullmq-unhandled-error-events

hotfix: stop unhandled BullMQ Redis errors from crashing the app

fix(backend): stop unhandled BullMQ Redis errors from crashing the app

The previous two crash fixes covered the Throttler's raw ioredis
client and QueueBootstrapService's blocking await, but the deploy
still crashed on the exact same "AUTH command / ReplyError" pattern —
this time from BullMQ itself. Both Queue and Worker extend
EventEmitter, and BullMQ's internal RedisConnection re-emits its
client's 'error' event onto them; with nothing listening at that
level, Node's default "throw if no error listener" behavior crashes
the process, same as the original Throttler bug — BullMQ creates
several of these connections internally (one per Queue, one per
Worker) that app code never constructs directly, so there was no
single place to attach a handler.

- Add @OnWorkerEvent('error') to AiQueueProcessor and
  MaintenanceQueueProcessor.
- Add .on('error', ...) to the injected Queue instances in
  AiJobsService and QueueBootstrapService.
- Add a process-level uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handler in
  main.ts as a last-resort net: log loudly and keep running rather
  than crash-loop. Given how many separate BullMQ connections exist
  and that three rounds of this same symptom have now shown up in
  different places, this is the only way to be confident we won't hit
  a fourth one somewhere unaudited. It doesn't silence anything and
  isn't a substitute for the targeted fixes above — it's a floor
  under all of them while Redis itself (Upstash's exhausted request
  quota) stays down.

hotfix: stop maintenance queue registration from blocking backend boot

fix(backend): stop maintenance queue registration from blocking boot

QueueBootstrapService.onModuleInit awaited two unguarded
maintenanceQueue.add() calls. onModuleInit hooks are awaited before
Nest calls app.listen(), so when Redis is failing (e.g. Upstash's
request quota being exhausted, as happened in production after the
last deploy), these calls rejecting with no catch meant the whole
bootstrap never completed and the HTTP server never started —
Render's health check then had nothing to connect to and marked the
deploy failed, even though the earlier Redis crash fix had already
stopped the process from actually crashing.

Wrap both calls in a try/catch: log and continue instead of blocking
startup. The repeatable jobs just won't be registered until Redis is
back, same as everything else that degrades gracefully when Redis is
unavailable.
